name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement refused its run
message: A scheduled statement on {{host.name}} refused its run, or could not run at all (broken): its slot is marked refused and the next runs as due, so the work of this one is not done. The server's log names the statement, the slot, the status and why, with the run's request_id; `statements` (or GET /_schema) shows its `last` mark. A guard unmet (412) is the statement saying so; a broken one (409) is mended by `create or replace statement`.

name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement's slot is held back
message: A scheduled statement's slot on {{host.name}} was refused by the state of its database -- a tenant at its quota (507), a lapsed lease, a storage error -- and is held: tried again as the data or the limit changes, or after a backoff of a minute doubling to fifteen. Nothing of it is lost while it is held, but nothing of it is done, and the next slot passes over it. `statements` shows `held` with the status and since when; the log names the first refusal.

name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement's mark is ahead of the clock
message: A scheduled statement's last mark on {{host.name}} stands ahead of the server's clock: the clock was stepped back behind a run, or a clock that was ahead ran it. Within an hour its slots wait for the clock to pass the mark; further ahead the schedule goes on from the clock and the slots the wrong clock ran run again as they come. Check the host's NTP. The audit log's `clock` line names the statement, the mark and the clock.

name: fennecdb: scheduled statements run late
message: Scheduled runs on {{host.name}} began more than two minutes past their slots (p99): a node's tenants due at one instant run one at a time, each behind the runs before it, and a restart runs a missed slot late. Lateness is no fault in itself -- `slot()` names the slot a run was for -- but a node always this late wants its tenants' schedules spread or fewer tenants.
